results.basis:
VERIFIED DIRECTLY BY THIS SESSION (2026-08-09), from two Federal Reserve sources plus the Federal Register record. Cleanest verbatim, from the Board's own press release of 2 July 2013 announcing the rule ("Federal Reserve Board approves final rule to help ensure banks maintain strong capital positions"), fetched in full: "The rule will implement in the United States the Basel III regulatory capital reforms from the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision and certain changes required by the Dodd-Frank Wall Street Reform and Consumer Protection Act." The adopting Federal Register notice carries the relationship in its own title -- "...Implementation of Basel III..." (FR doc. 2013-21653, 11 October 2013, OCC and Board) -- and its SUMMARY names the Basel Committee publication by title, that the proposals "reflected agreements reached by the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (BCBS) in 'Basel III: A Global Regulatory Framework for More Resilient Banks and Banking Systems' (Basel III)". PROVENANCE CAVEAT, per Research.1.md sec.2: that last sentence is reported by this session's fetch tool, which truncated its own direct quotation of the SUMMARY at 125 characters ("Basel III: A Global Regulatory Framework for More Resilient Banks and Banking Sys") and supplied the surrounding clause as reconstruction rather than as a clean verbatim read. The press-release sentence above is a clean read and is what the edge rests on; a successor with a working PDF route should replace the SUMMARY quotation with a verbatim one from govinfo (FR-2013-10-11, 78 FR 62018). WEAKER THAN THE OSFI EDGE IN ONE RESPECT, stated plainly: OSFI's Chapter 1 says of itself that it "is drawn from" the Basel Framework, so the dependency is asserted inside the standing document. Here the Basel naming sits in the instrument that ADOPTED the CFR part, not in the codified text of part 217, which does not mention Basel. This is adoption-preamble evidence, which the corpus accepts for regulations, not in-document methodology prose. NOT an instance of trap 5a: "implement in the United States" is an implementation claim, not a comparability claim.

CLEAN VERBATIM READ SUBSTITUTED, 2026-08-09 (closing G.64.md cheap check 4). The PROVENANCE CAVEAT above is resolved: govinfo's HTML rendition of the same document (FR-2013-10-11, 78 FR 62018, package FR-2013-10-11, document 2013-21653) was fetched directly and returned the sentence complete, with no truncation. Correcting the earlier session's own attribution in passing: the sentence is not in the SUMMARY block but in the Introduction section, footnote 2 -- 'The proposed rules, in part, reflected agreements reached by the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (BCBS) in ``Basel III: A Global Regulatory Framework for More Resilient Banks and Banking Systems'' (Basel III).' (double-backtick/double-quote pairs are govinfo's plain-text rendering of typeset quotation marks, reproduced as in the source.) This is now a second, independent, cleanly-read confirmation alongside the press-release sentence the edge already rests on -- it does not change what the edge asserts, only removes the earlier read's uncertainty about its own completeness. REPOINTED 2026-09-04 (Thomas ruling) from bis-basel-framework to basel-iii: the Board press release names the Basel III regulatory capital reforms and never names the Basel Framework, so the citation now matches the artefact the document actually names.

targetReport.title: Basel III
targetReport.publisher: Basel Committee on Banking Supervision, Bank for International Settlements
targetReport.description: The package of bank capital, leverage, liquidity and risk-coverage standards agreed by the Basel Committee after the 2007-09 crisis. BIS's own page states: "Basel III is an internationally agreed set of measures developed by the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision in response to the financial crisis of 2007-09." Issued in phases — the December 2010 framework revised June 2011, the Liquidity Coverage Ratio (2013), the Net Stable Funding Ratio (2014), the December 2017 finalisation of the remaining reforms, and the January 2019 market-risk minimum requirements. Separate from bis-basel-framework, which is the consolidated compilation that now carries it: "The Basel III reforms have now been integrated into the consolidated Basel Framework, which comprises all of the current and forthcoming standards of the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision." Minted 2026-09-04 on Thomas's ruling. The reason is evidential, not taxonomic: three of the five edges then pointing at bis-basel-framework quote documents that name Basel III specifically and never name the Basel Framework, so the corpus was recording a citation the sources do not make. Deliberately NOT given part_of: bis-basel-framework (Thomas, 2026-09-04) — the containment is real and is recorded here in prose, but the node stands alone in the schema. Country code is INT; the schema's international option is used here as on the other BIS/IMF standards.
targetReport.cadence_note: Nominal, as on sna-2008 and imf-gfsm — the enum has no bucket for a standard. results.window: It establishes an integrated regulatory capital framework that addresses shortcomings in capital requirements, particularly for larger, internationally active banking organizations, that became apparent during the recent financial crisis. The rule will implement in the United States the Basel III regulatory capital reforms from the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision and certain changes required by the Dodd-Frank Wall Street Reform and Consumer Protection Act. targetReport.title: Censo Demográfico
targetReport.publisher: Instituto Brasileiro de Geografia e Estatística (IBGE)
targetReport.description: Decennial population and housing census providing the most comprehensive demographic, social and economic profile of the Brazilian population. The 2022 Census (13th operation) collected data from 1 August 2022 to 28 May 2023 (with subsequent revisions). Results released progressively by theme (population and households, literacy, indigenous and quilombola populations, urban characteristics, sample results on labour, education, fertility, etc.). Primary source for population totals, municipal population, demographic structure and many derived indicators used across the statistical system and for inter-governmental transfers.
targetReport.cadence_note: Nominally decennial; the last two were 2010 and 2022.

release_schedule.rule: Lei 8.184/1991: "A periodicidade dos Censos Demográficos, Censo Agropecuário e Censos Econômicos será fixada por ato do Poder Executivo, não podendo exceder a dez anos" (periodicity of the Demographic Census shall be fixed by act of the Executive Power, not to exceed ten years). In practice IBGE has run the census roughly every 10 years (1970, 1980, 1991, 2000, 2010, 2022 — the 2020 edition was postponed to 2022 due to the pandemic).
release_schedule.note: No formal Executive decree fixing the exact 2030 date/collection period has been located; IBGE's own president has publicly referred to work on a "Censo 2030" (discussing hybrid/technological collection methods), and a Brazilian news outlet (Estado de Minas, Jan 2026) states "a próxima grande contagem da população brasileira está prevista para 2030". This restores the original decennial cycle (2000, 2010, 2020→2022 delayed, 2030) rather than counting 10 years forward from the delayed 2022 edition (which would suggest 2032). Exact month/day of collection is not yet published.

results.basis: VERIFIED DIRECTLY (Volume 3 -- Financial Statements PDF fetched from aucklandcouncil.govt.nz with curl, 152 pages, pypdf-extracted, this session). Self-classification: "the council has designated itself and the group as public benefit entities (PBEs) and applies New Zealand Tier 1 PBE Accounting Standards. These standards are based on International Public Sector Accounting Standards (IPSAS), with amendments for the New Zealand environment." Named by exact title in the accounting-policy-changes note, on the same structural footing as this slice's Wellington edge into the same target (Wellington's own citation is likewise from a 'changes to accounting standards' note, not a primary compliance clause): "The 2024 Omnibus Amendments issued in October 2024 include updates to PBE IPSAS 1 Presentation of Financial Reports to clarify the principles for classifying liabilities as current or non-current. The amendments are effective from reporting periods beginning on or after 1 January 2026 with early adoption permitted." CHAIN GENERALISES: this is the second New Zealand council in the corpus naming PBE IPSAS 1 by exact title, confirming the finding is not a Wellington idiosyncrasy.

targetReport.title: PBE IPSAS 1 Presentation of Financial Reports
targetReport.publisher: New Zealand Accounting Standards Board / External Reporting Board (XRB)
targetReport.description: The presentation standard for Tier 1 and Tier 2 public benefit entities, which is what New Zealand councils report under. Like XRB A1, it names no local authority: grep of its full 54 pages returns 0 hits for 'local authority', 'Local Government Act' and 'Public Audit Act'. The only local-government hook in its text is the word 'ratepayers' in the list of users of general purpose financial reports (para 3), which is not a scope binding. The binding is achieved instead by a statutory chain outside the standard — see the `nz-wellington-annual-report` edge.
targetReport.cadence_note: Issued September 2014; version read this session incorporates amendments to 31 January 2022 with further amendments effective 1 January 2026.

release_schedule.note: PBE IPSAS 1 is an accounting standard (not a periodic statistical report). XRB amends it irregularly via omnibus amendment packages as IPSASB updates the underlying international standard or NZ policy changes require it. Original issue November 2014; most recent substantive update is the October 2024 omnibus amendments (compiled to March 2025), effective for periods beginning 1 January 2026, with a prior amendment in May 2023 (audit fee disclosures). The XRB website states no fixed review cycle or forthcoming release date. The releases_per_year=0.2 figure on file (implying a ~5-year cadence) is not supported by any stated rule; amendment timing is genuinely irregular and driven by IPSASB/policy developments, not a fixed schedule.

targetReport.title: Consumer Price Index Manual: Concepts and Methods
targetReport.publisher: IMF, ILO, OECD, Eurostat, UNECE and the World Bank
targetReport.description: The internationally agreed manual of concepts, methods and practice for compiling a consumer price index. Jointly published by six international organisations and managed by the IMF; the 2020 edition updates the 2004 ILO-managed Consumer Price Index Manual: Theory and Practice. Country code is CA only because the schema offers no international option — the publisher is a consortium of international agencies.
targetReport.cadence_note: Revised roughly once a generation — editions in 1989, 2004 and 2020. Not an annual release; releases_per_year is nominal so the pulse rate reads as near-static.

release_schedule.note: No release calendar or stated periodicity exists. The Manual has been issued only three times: 1989 (ILO, 'Consumer Price Indices: An ILO Manual'), 2004 ('Consumer Price Index Manual: Theory and Practice'), and 2020 ('Consumer Price Index Manual: Concepts and Methods'), each ~15-16 years apart. The IMF's own page for this report is titled 'Update of the Consumer Price Index Manual' and explains the 2020 edition was produced because 'methods and best practices have continued to evolve' since 2004, following requests from the 2014 UNECE-ILO CPI Experts Meeting -- i.e., updates are triggered by inter-agency expert consensus, not a fixed schedule. No next-edition date or working-group timeline is published. This is consistent with the corpus's very low releases_per_year (0.06, i.e. roughly once per 16 years).

results.basis: Welfare and Institutions Code §11453(a) provides that the aid amounts "shall be adjusted annually" and that "the cost-of-living adjustment shall be calculated by the Department of Finance based on the changes in the California Necessities Index, which as used in this section means the weighted average changes for food, clothing, fuel, utilities, rent, and transportation for low-income consumers". Adjusted amounts are rounded to the nearest dollar and take effect July 1.

targetReport.title: California Necessities Index (CNI)
targetReport.description: A statutorily defined weighted price index for food, clothing, fuel, utilities, rent and transportation for low-income consumers, computed by the Department of Finance from BLS CPI components using the area weights of the California CPI. A purpose-built poverty-basket index that exists because the general CPI was judged not to describe what a welfare recipient buys.
targetReport.cadence_note: Weakly anchored on purpose: the statutory duty to compute the index is clear (W&I Code §§11453, 12201) but no standing Department of Finance page publishing the series could be found, and the figure surfaces inside budget documents and county letters instead. The URL is the closest publisher landing page, not a verified index page.

entries.covers: Next statutory annual CNI-based adjustment effective date

release_schedule.rule: Welfare and Institutions Code Section 11453: annual adjustments to grants based on the California Necessities Index, computed by the Department of Finance from CPI-based cost data for food, clothing, fuel/utilities, rent, and transportation, "shall become effective July 1 of each year."
release_schedule.note: The DOF page given as the corpus URL (dof.ca.gov/forecasting/economics/economic-indicators/) does not mention the CNI at all — no calendar or CNI reference found there. Per Welf. & Inst. Code 11453, CNI-based adjustments take effect July 1 each year; July 1, 2026 has already passed as of today (2026-08-11), so the next occurrence is July 1, 2027. Note a complication found via LAO (Aug 2025, https://www.lao.ca.gov/reports/2025/5065/Updating-CA-Necessities-Index-081425.pdf): BLS discontinued publishing the specific consumer expenditure data the CNI formula relies on, making the index impossible to compute under the old formula starting with the 2026-27 budget. A 2026 budget trailer bill (Gov. Code 13074.1, see https://trailerbill.dof.ca.gov/public/trailerBill/pdf/1337) subsequently authorized DOF to use "a reasonable estimate" of missing data for such cost-of-living/annual-adjustment calculations, with the resulting calculation deemed final — which appears intended to preserve continuity of the annual July 1 CNI adjustment cycle going forward, though I found no DOF page explicitly confirming a computed CNI value for July 2027 yet.

targetReport.description: The metropolitan-area CPI-U for the Houston core based statistical area, and the index the City of Houston uses to adjust its property tax revenue cap. Published bimonthly rather than monthly, in even months, and not seasonally adjusted. The area has been renamed twice — from Houston-Galveston-Brazoria, and again under the 2023 delineation — while the underlying series identifier stayed put.
targetReport.cadence_note: Bimonthly, which matters less than it looks: the City reads the annual average for the preceding calendar year, so a six-a-year series still yields a usable yearly figure.

release_schedule.note: BLS Southwest Information Office publishes Houston-The Woodlands-Sugar Land CPI bimonthly (every other month: Feb, Apr, Jun, Aug, Oct, Dec), consistent with releases_per_year=6 on file. The July 14, 2026 news release (covering June 2026 data) explicitly states the next release date.

results.window:
The FY2026 property tax revenue estimate is derived according to Proposition 1 and Proposition H. The Finance
Department applied the 2024 inflation rate of 2.4641% and population estimates as of July 1, 2024 of 3.28% to
arrive to a new revenue estimate of $1.50 billion. This revenue is an increase of $123.1 million or 8.91% from the
estimated FY2025 revenue of $1.38 billion.

results.basis: The same footnote: "Population numbers based upon the US Census Bureau estimate most recently published when deciding limits of each respective year's property tax revenue budget increase", with the City reporting "population estimates as of July 1, 2024 of 3.28%". The charter text as quoted in the City's financial report says "the City's population growth (as determined by the U.S. Census)", so the specific series is again the administrative implementation.

targetReport.title: Population Estimates Program (Vintage Estimates)
targetReport.description: Annual estimates of the resident population for the nation, states and counties, produced between decennial censuses. Each vintage starts from the most recent decennial census count and carries it forward with administrative records on births, deaths and net international migration. Distinct from the decennial census itself: the census is a count, this is a model built on top of the count, and it is the model rather than the count that most federal programmes and surveys actually use year to year.
targetReport.cadence_note: A new vintage is released each December for the nation and states, with county and sub-county detail following through the following spring.

release_schedule.note: Stated target is 'December' for the first release, but the Vintage 2025 national release actually slipped to Jan 27, 2026 — treat month-level dates as plan, not guarantee.
